title: Best Cordless Leaf Blowers UK
short: Cordless leaf blowers and blower/vacuum combos compared by blow speed, noise and battery life, from compact lightweight models to powerful garden clearers.
intro: A leaf blower's real test is whether it shifts heavy, wet leaves without running out of charge halfway through, not just its top blow speed. This guide compares blowers tested by Expert Reviews against wet tree leaves, dry hedge clippings and debris on both tarmac and lawn.

products.name: AdvancedLeafBlower 36V-750
products.best_for: Buyers who just want maximum blowing power without vacuum features
products.summary: Expert Reviews found even the heaviest, wettest leaves couldn't hold against its maximum power setting, blasting entangled leaves free from ground cover plants. An easy under-thumb power dial lets you dial back for lighter work, though it's a little noisier and heavier than rivals, using Bosch's less common 36V battery system.
pros: Powerful enough for the heaviest, wettest leaves

products.name: WG583E
products.best_for: Buyers who want to collect and mulch leaves, not just scatter them
products.key_spec: Convertible blower/vacuum, 35l collection bag, up to 209km/h blow speed
products.summary: A beefy convertible unit that Expert Reviews found easy to switch between blowing and vacuuming, sucking up big piles of damp leaves in seconds and shredding them to barely fill the 35l bag. It even tackled moss and conifer clippings without issue, though battery life at full power is short.
pros: Genuinely capable at both blowing and vacuuming
Neatly shreds and compacts collected leaves
Handles big, damp leaves and moss
cons: Short battery life at full power (~10 minutes)

products.name: PowerJet 18V P4A
products.best_for: Budget buyers who already own Power For All batteries
products.key_spec: 18V battery, 100km/h blow speed, detachable precision nozzle
products.summary: Sits between Bosch's powerful model and lightweight compacts, giving Expert Reviews plenty of oomph for a soggy lawn or driveway while staying easy on the arms. It's surprisingly quiet at under 75dB, with a clear LED charge indicator, though battery and charger are sold separately if you don't already own the Power For All system.
pros: Good value if you already have Power For All batteries

products.name: WG543E
products.best_for: Buyers who want a lightweight, easily stored blower
products.key_spec: Under 80cm long, 1.79kg, air amplifier technology, up to 209km/h
products.summary: So light and compact that Expert Reviews doubted its power at first glance, but air amplifier technology drives more air through the tube than expected, easily separating soggy leaves from a lawn. Noise levels are low at around 69dB, though battery and charger are sold separately from the tool.
pros: Very light and compact, usable one-handed

products.name: BLV 18-200
products.badge: Best combi for ease of use
products.best_for: Buyers who want simple one-switch blow/vacuum switching with boost mode
products.key_spec: 45L collection bag, built-in mulching, one-switch mode change, boost mode
products.summary: Needs no tricky configuration, with a single flick switching between blowing and vacuuming, plus little wheels to help support the unit while collecting. Expert Reviews found the 45L bag and mulching meant you'd likely run out of charge before needing to empty it, though it can't match the most powerful blowers for raw force without engaging boost mode.
pros: Effective boost mode for tougher debris
cons: Expensive, especially with battery/charger sold separately

guide.a: A blower-only model, like the Bosch or Worx WG543E here, is simpler and usually lighter, good for scattering or piling leaves for later collection. A combo, like the Worx WG583E or Kärcher here, sucks up and shreds leaves into a collection bag, saving a separate raking or sweeping step, at the cost of extra weight and complexity.

guide.q: What blow speed do I actually need?
guide.a: For light, dry leaves and general tidying, 100-160km/h is usually enough. For heavier, wet leaves or larger gardens with trees like horse chestnut or sycamore, look for 200km/h or more, like the Bosch, Worx WG543E or Kärcher here, to avoid leaves simply not moving.

Most cordless leaf blowers use an 18V motor and battery, which is fine for small to medium gardens. For a big garden or trees that shed heavy leaves in volume, a 36V or 40V model, like the Bosch here, gives noticeably more power at the cost of extra weight.

guide.q: Is it worth sticking to one battery brand system?
guide.a: Yes, if you already own or plan to buy other cordless garden tools. Battery alliances like Bosch's Power For All let 18V batteries work across tools from Bosch, Gardena, Flymo and Husqvarna, so checking compatibility with tools you already own, like the Gardena here, can save buying a spare battery and charger.
